questions.question: Two years ago, T was twice as old as P. P is thrice as old as R. In five years, P will be 29. What is the present age of T?
questions.solution:
Given: Two years ago, T was twice as old as P. P is thrice as old as R. In five years, P will be 29. 

According to the question,

Two years ago, T was twice as old as P.

 
• T - 2 = 2 × (P - 2); _________(i)

At present, P is thrice as old as R.

 
• P = 3 × R; ____________(ii)

In five years, P will be 29. 

 
• P + 5 = 29
 
• P = 29 - 5 = 24 years

Now, by substituting the age of P, we get,

 
• T - 2 = 2 × (P - 2)
 
• T - 2 = 2 × (24 - 2)
 
• T - 2 = 2 × 22
 
• T = 44 + 2
 
• T = 46 years

Hence, the present age of T is **46 years.**

questions.question: Which of the given equations is correctly balanced if ‘A’ means ‘+’, ‘B’ means ‘–’, ‘C’ means ‘×’, and ‘D’ means ‘÷’?

Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number.

16 : 256 :: 21 : ? :: 19 : 361
questions.solution:
Given: 16 : 256 :: 21 : ? :: 19 : 361

The logic followed here is:

16 : 256 → 16² = 256

And,

19 : 361 → 19² = 361

Similarly,

21 : ? → 21² = 441

Hence, **441 **is the correct answer.
